proven_conclusions.claim: The 54.12 zero was not merely stored between wheel updates. The driver wheel-update path consumed cmd2516 at 54.121 and issued paired zero-directed slew targets.

OnUpdate samples world odometry, publishes the odom message, then selects the command, reads joint-rim feedback and calls wheel SetParam. Thus the first violating odom stamped54.155 precedes that same update's resumed pure-turn target write.
proven_conclusions.implication: The first54.155 speed breach cannot have been produced by the new wheel write issued later in that same update. This does not isolate the cause among earlier actuation/history or braking-phase plant response.

proven_conclusions.claim: The stateless common-fraction limiter starts from unequal measured joint-rim feedback. When desired rims are both zero, one shared alpha shrinks both measured values; it does not impose equal wheel magnitudes or zero mean rim speed during deceleration.
proven_conclusions.implication: The original zero consumed a real paired braking step with unequal issued rim magnitudes. This algebra alone does not prove body drift, slip, actuator dynamics or solver cause.

proven_conclusions.claim: The source54.155 body velocity is read from the native model WorldLinearVel and yaw-rotated into base_footprint. The recorded planar norm0.02020358683181293 exceeds the unchanged0.01 settled-turn bound; it is not inferred from received-map/TF displacement.

At54.155 the measured rim pair already has common component0.01379669701396559. The resumed requested v0,w0.8 fits the per-wheel slew budget (alpha1) and issues symmetric rims[0.1148,-0.1148]. Neither the symmetric new target nor its stored command retroactively changes the preceding body-velocity sample.

limitations_and_unproven_claims: SetParam calls and the following actuation audit show the driver issued targets. Return values are not audited; this artifact does not independently prove successful physics-engine target acceptance, exact torque, tracking or no slip.

The drive audit contains no per-record wall timestamp. Cross-file causal ordering here is established by exact source-time and verified driver source call order, not by comparing cross-file record_sequence values.
A source-stamped odom message can be received while the guard log clock still shows an earlier paused boundary; this does not invert the driver's internal sample-before-write order.
Observed rim feedback asymmetry predates the zero pulse; it is not evidence that the paired limiter violated its common-fraction formula or per-wheel1m/s^2 bound.

Body planar velocity and averaged joint-rim velocity are distinct native measurements. Their difference does not, by itself, establish slip, contact impulse, caster, solver, controller, geometry or friction root cause.
Temporal adjacency to a consumed braking step is not a controlled demonstration that braking causes the violation or that continuous pure turn would pass.
No-contact records, if present elsewhere, cannot serve as proof that the settled-turn model or all safety gates pass.
